html:
António de Oliveira Salazar was the dictator of Portugal from 1932 to 1968. He founded the Estado Novo, the New State, the longest-lasting dictatorship in western Europe.

A professor of economics at Coimbra, he was called in as finance minister by the military rulers in 1928 and balanced the budget. As prime minister he built a Catholic, conservative and corporatist state under the constitution of 1933, with censorship and a secret police, the PIDE. His motto was God, Fatherland, Family.

He kept Portugal neutral in the Second World War, and refused to give up the colonies, which led to the colonial wars in Angola, Guinea and Mozambique from 1961. Portugal stayed poor, and many emigrated. He was disabled by a stroke in 1968, and his regime fell in the Carnation Revolution of 1974.
sum: António de Oliveira Salazar was the dictator of Portugal from 1932 to 1968. He founded the Estado Novo, the New State, the longest-lasting dictatorship in western Europe.
